why_relevant: Large global tender database with a searchable Hungary section and daily custom email alerts, claiming very large live-tender and private-tender-result volumes. Its claim to hold private tender results is the interesting part for banking - if genuine it covers non-public buyer activity - but the claim is vendor marketing and unvalidated.

Country-dedicated commercial tender portal for Hungary with cheap subscription tiers and a 1-day free trial; BidDetail runs a parallel Hungary section. Country-dedicated framing makes it a convenient recall benchmark, though these portals are generally TED-derived rather than adding below-threshold depth.

source_subtype: global commercial tender aggregator with open dated listings
why_relevant: Aggregator that publishes dated, paginated public lists of Hungarian tenders. The date-partitioned public listing structure is unusually crawl-friendly, making it a cheap redundancy feed for detecting notices even without a subscription.

source_subtype: TED-derived aggregator with indexable per-notice pages
why_relevant: Aggregator that publishes individual TED-derived notices at stable, indexable per-notice URLs (observed pattern includes a TED reference in the slug). Because its notice pages are search-engine indexed, it acts as a practical back-door search layer over TED content, sometimes easier to query than TED's own interface.

EU-supported 'one-stop shop for tendering across Europe' offering its service free. A free EU-backed aggregator is unusually attractive for sustained monitoring since there is no licence barrier to ingestion; Hungarian coverage depth was not confirmed in this pass.

Cross-border tender platform aimed at SMEs bidding in foreign EU markets, explicitly framed around removing the language/market barrier. Relevant as the category of aggregator most likely to translate Hungarian-language notices into English, which affects whether a non-Hungarian competitor can see and act on HU banking tenders.

source_subtype: vendor marketing article pointing to a tender alert product
why_relevant: Vendor content describing an AI-summarisation tender alert product with unlimited Hungary email alerts. Recorded as a pointer because the product's own canonical domain was not confirmed in this pass - only a marketing article on gtbc.net was observed. Worth resolving because AI-summarised tender documents would materially cut analyst effort on Hungarian-language specifications.

Hungarian procurement-trade article enumerating tenderértesítő / tender hírlevél services and the vocabulary around them. Valuable as a snowball pointer: it is written in the practitioner's own terminology and names services that generic search does not rank, helping extend the HU glossary for this cell.

Leading Hungarian business/finance daily; covers bank strategy, vendor selections, municipal account-holder switches and treasury policy changes that drive banking/payments sourcing. Has an English edition (portfolio.hu/en). Frequently first to report deal values and context that never appear in formal award notices.

Long-running Hungarian economic daily with a dedicated penz-es-tokepiac (money & capital markets) desk; reports bank technology programmes, AI/digital rollouts across OTP, MBH, K&H, CIB, Granit, and executive/vendor changes that signal upcoming sourcing.

Hungarian B2B IT business portal that specifically covers public-sector and financial-sector IT procurement, framework agreements, central procurement supplier lists and core-banking replacements (e.g. MKB core system swap). One of the few outlets naming IT suppliers and contract values.

Computerworld Hungary ceased publication in Dec 2023 and was relaunched by Project029 as ComputerTrends; it remains the Hungarian CIO-focused B2B IT magazine covering enterprise/bank IT projects, vendor wins and CIO interviews. IMPORTANT correction to the cell brief: 'Computerworld HU' as such no longer exists.

Veteran Hungarian IT news site with enterprise/telco/finance coverage; useful for vendor-side announcements and integrator news relating to Hungarian bank systems, and as a historical archive back to the 2000s.

Hungary's main fintech blog/portal; covers card acceptance, softPOS, POS terminals, qvik/instant payment rollouts, MNB payment statistics and — critically — named vendor selections such as OTP Bank's new account-management and lending core system. Often reports private-bank sourcing that has no procurement channel.

Second Hungarian fintech news outlet; profiles new bank builds and technology stacks (e.g. AI-driven bank PeakX), useful for spotting greenfield banking projects that will generate payment-infrastructure sourcing.

Major independent weekly/news site; breaks stories on large IT tenders (e.g. the HUF 390bn state IT tender) and on bank sector politics. Its tag pages act as pointer indexes into topics and companies.

G7 (now hosted at Telex) is Hungary's sharpest economics-analysis desk on procurement mechanics — single-bidder tenders, framework re-tendering, risk allocation. Explains why contracts were structured a given way and identifies losing/absent bidders.

Hungarian business news daily named in the cell scope; covers bank corporate news, contract announcements and financial-sector supplier stories. Complementary de-duplication source against Portfolio/VG.

High-volume mainstream news site that amplifies and adds official reactions to tender/procurement stories broken by G7 and Átlátszó; useful for capturing counter-statements from contracting authorities and winners.

Independent news site that aggregates and follows up on large IT tender stories (e.g. the HUF 390bn Digital Government Agency IT tender), often naming winning suppliers. Acts as a fast pointer into HVG/G7/Átlátszó originals.

Business news site that systematically publishes municipal banking mandate outcomes — e.g. MBH Bank becoming Veszprém's exclusive account-holding institution following a tender. High-signal for A2 municipal banking contract awards.

Press-release distribution/news site carrying corporate announcements including bank municipal-mandate wins (e.g. MBH Bank as Debrecen's exclusive account-holding institution). Useful as an early, structured signal of awarded banking mandates.

Regional Debrecen outlet reporting the city's bank switch — an example of the county/city-level press layer that covers municipal banking tenders never picked up nationally. Template for a wider regional-press panel.

source_name: Municipal own-websites as local news channel (example: kisvarda.hu hírek)
why_relevant: Municipalities publish 'tájékoztató bankváltásról' notices naming the outgoing and incoming account-holding bank and effective dates — a direct, primary confirmation of an awarded banking mandate, typically before any trade-press mention.

The main English-language Hungarian business publication; covers bank corporate deals, vendor partnerships and market entries for an international audience. Valuable for English-language naming of vendors and deal values usable without translation.

English mirror/selection of Portfolio's banking and economy coverage; used to cross-check Hungarian-language deal reporting and to obtain quotable English phrasing of contract and ownership transactions.

Trade press about the Hungarian media industry itself — the authoritative way to know which trade titles still exist, who owns them and which have folded or rebranded (it documented Computerworld's closure and ComputerTrends' launch). Essential for keeping this source panel accurate over time.
